summary: Conrad M. Arensberg was an Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934). He held a post at Columbia University (~1946–1979) and taught Morton Klass.

Constance Kassor works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a BA from Smith College under Jay L. Garfield and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining Smith College's faculty (attested 2014).
Constance Powell Chin works in religious studies, history, and archaeology. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constantin Regamey was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Warsaw and Paris under Schayer, Turczyński, Przyluski, and Lalou, and later taught at Warsaw, Lausanne, and Fribourg, also serving as president of the Swiss Asia Society.

Corinna May Lhoir specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a doctoral student at Ghent University and Hamburg University, where she also serves as a lecturer and yoga studies program coordinator.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a master's degree under Jaap den Hollander and completed his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2002 under Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Remonstrant Seminary and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts as a Remonstrant pastor and professor, and as professor of the history of religions at Leiden University (1873, 1877–1901).

Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Raniero Gnoli and Giuseppe Tucci, taught Cristina Pecchia and Filippo Marsili, and served as professor at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).
Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and was mentored by Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She has held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge, and held posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 2002), including curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).
Craig Preston works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981).

Cristina Pecchia is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a PhD at Sapienza University of Rome under Gnoli, Torella, and Pensa, and studied at Vienna under Steinkellner. She has held posts at IKGA and the University of Vienna.

Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2004.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed a D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (2003–2009) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).
Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held posts as an assistant professor at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies and Sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, and served as adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
